title: Hybrid de novo genome assembly using Illumina, PacBio and Hi-C sequencing data
author: Hansheng Zhao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rf4d3qw

steps.title: Filter low-quality reads
steps.instruction: Use NGS QC Toolkit version 2.3.3 on Linux CentOS 6 with default parameters to discard any read where more than 40 % of bases have quality score Q < 13.

steps.title: Correct PacBio reads
steps.instruction: Run MECAT (release 20170627) on Linux CentOS 6 with parameters -x 0 -i 0 -t 60 -r 0.8 -a 1000 -c 5 -l 2000 to generate error‑corrected PacBio reads.

steps.title: Assemble Illumina PE reads
steps.instruction: Execute Platanus version 1.2.4 on Linux CentOS 6 using the filtered paired‑end Illumina reads; allow automatic k‑mer size optimization to produce contig.fa.

steps.title: Build hybrid scaffolds with DBG2OLC
steps.instruction: Run DBG2OLC (release 20150611) on Linux CentOS 6, providing the corrected PacBio reads and the Platanus contigs (contig.fa) with the following options: LD 0, K 17, KmerCovTh 4, MinOverlap 25, AdaptiveTh 0.007, RemoveChimera 1, output file scaffold.fa.

steps.title: Polish DBG2OLC consensus
steps.instruction: Perform consensus polishing of the DBG2OLC assembly (as described in the DBG2OLC documentation) to improve assembly quality before downstream scaffolding.

steps.title: Extend scaffolds with SSPACE
steps.instruction: Apply SSPACE version 3.0 on Linux CentOS 6 using the mate‑pair (MP) reads to elongate the polished scaffolds.

steps.title: Close gaps with GapCloser
steps.instruction: Run GapCloser version 1.12 on Linux CentOS 6 with the Illumina data to fill gaps in the SSPACE‑extended scaffolds.

steps.title: Fill remaining gaps with PBJelly
steps.instruction: Execute PBJelly (release 20150824) on Linux CentOS 6 using the PacBio data to further close gaps in the GapCloser output.

steps.title: Evaluate Hi‑C data quality
steps.instruction: Assess and filter the Hi‑C dataset with HiC‑Pro version 2.8.0_devel on Linux CentOS 6 to obtain a set of valid Hi‑C contacts.

steps.title: Generate chromosome‑level scaffolds
steps.instruction: Process the validated Hi‑C data together with the assembled scaffolds using the 3D‑DNA pipeline (version 170123) on Linux CentOS 6 to produce chromosome‑level scaffolds.

steps.title: Visualize contact maps in JuiceBox
steps.instruction: Load the 3D‑DNA output into JuiceBox version 1.5.2 on Linux CentOS 6 to visualize Hi‑C contact maps and manually curate scaffolds if needed.
